name: Biophilia Hypothesis
short_description: The innate human tendency to affiliate with other living systems and natural processes, manifesting as preference for natural materials, patterns, and living elements in the built environment.

components.name: Nature Affinity & Implicit Evaluation
components.description: Rapid, automatic positive affective response to natural environmental features, predating conscious evaluation.

components.name: Nature Exposure Multi-Pathway
components.description: Nature exposure drives stress reduction through multiple parallel neurobiological pathways simultaneously.

components.name: Material-Haptic Response
components.description: Haptic exploration of natural materials (wood, stone) generates positive affective responses distinct from synthetic materials.

components.name: Fractal & Visual Pattern Response
components.description: Visual scene statistics matching natural 1/f fractal scaling reduce prediction error and promote fluent processing.

design_implications: Incorporate natural materials (wood, stone, living walls) over synthetic surfaces.
Use biomorphic forms and fractal patterns at 1/f scaling in surface textures and facades.
Provide direct visual access to vegetation, water features, or sky from workspaces.
Integrate multisensory nature cues: natural sounds, daylight variation, natural ventilation.

confidence_intervals.note: Meta-analytic estimates for nature exposure on stress reduction and mood improvement.

basis: Inferred from molecule name: bridges biophilia
